subject: Post-call: Performance SLOs and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ben Jacobs <ben.jacobs@novaretail.com>, Claire Huang <claire.huang@novaretail.com>
Cc: 
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Performance SLOs and next steps

Thanks for the time today - great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Recap of requirements you shared:
- Latency: target p95 <= 250ms for interactive search/chat flows; p50 target ~90-120ms
- Throughput: sustained ~3k requests/minute during peak window (approx 50 rps)
- Concurrency: expected concurrency up to ~80 concurrent users across two regions (we should confirm regional split)
- Streaming: yes - partial token streaming required for perceived latency on the chat UI
- Consistency: strong preference for deterministic outputs for reranking stage (model variant may be pinned)

Cost/performance levers we discussed (high-level):
- Continuous batching: reduces per-token overhead at the cost of small latency increases; can be tuned per-route
- Prefix/KV caching: large win if many requests share common prompts (e.g., product descriptions, system prompt)
- Quantization profiles: 8-bit and 4-bit tradeoffs - aggressive quantization reduces cost but can affect quality on some prompts
- Model variants: smaller models for low-latency/reranking, larger for long-form generation or higher accuracy

Proposed next steps:
1) Please share a 30-60 minute sample of production traffic (anonymized) or synthetic profile - helps us mirror token distribution and prompt shapes. (Ben/Claire)
2) I'll loop in Rishi (SE) to scope a short perf run with your sample traffic - baseline + 2 tuning passes (batching + quant).
3) Deliverable: perf matrix showing p50/p95 latency, throughput, and cost estimates across 3 model/quant profiles.

I've attached a brief model matrix that shows expected tradeoffs across common Redwood variants. If this plan sounds good I'll schedule the perf run for next week.

Thanks,

Ben - perfect, thanks for the sample. Looping in Rishi (SE) and Priyom (Perf lead) to scope the run and recommend concrete configuration tests.

Short answers to your quant question and what we'll test: 
- Quantization impact: 8-bit (int8/fp8 variants) typically gives ~1.5-2x throughput improvement with minimal quality regression on discriminative/short tasks. 4-bit (int4) can give ~3-4x cost reduction but the risk of small accuracy drift increases, especially on generation-heavy prompts. For reranking/discriminative scoring we usually see small/no regression on 8-bit; with 4-bit we recommend an eval prompt-set to validate.

Planned perf test matrix (what we'll run):
1) Baseline: your sample traffic against our default "chronos-13B" model (float32) - measure p50/p95, token throughput, and cost
2) Quantization pass: chronos-13B-8bit and chronos-13B-4bit - measure latency delta and quality on a small eval set you approve
3) Model-variant pass: chronos-13B-8bit vs chronos-7B-int4 vs chronos-3B-int4 - tradeoffs for latency/cost
4) Batching/caching tuning: continuous batching window (10-50ms), request coalescing, and prefix KV cache benefits (we'll measure hit-rate sims)
5) Streaming behavior: enable chunked output streaming to measure effective frontend-perceived latency (important for chat)

Operational notes: 
- Continuous batching: we'll tune target batch latency to keep p95 under 250ms while reducing per-token cost - expect 10-30% cost savings depending on request shape.
- KV/Prefix caching: if your rerank/search uses repeated system prompts or product snippets, even modest cache hit rates (20-40%) can cut token counts significantly.
- Fallbacks: we'll show a model-fallback policy (auto-route to 7B variant under load) to preserve availability while keeping quality acceptable.

Next steps: 
- Rishi/Priyom: can you take the attached sample and propose a 3-day perf calendar?
- Ben/Claire: confirm a short eval prompt set (10-20 queries) we can use to validate quality across quant profiles.

If that works I'll put calendar invites on everyone's schedule and start the baseline run.
